This report details findings from an analysis of the QFS signal data, focusing on the properties of the QFS-area in the context of the collaboration's results.

The rise of online news has been fueled by the personalization of the internet, 
which has also enabled the tracking of online online news consumption patterns. 
However, a significant portion of research has highlighted the decline in online 
news reliability and objectivity in recent years. As a result, current online 
news recommender systems frequently incorporate contextual information to capture 
user personality traits and emotional states. Yet, they often neglect another 
crucial aspect - political division. This study investigates online news 
consumption from a political perspective and reveals substantial political 
division within user reading behavior. Specifically, it finds that user interests 
in online news sources are highly polarized, reflecting distinct personality 
and ideological profiles. This discovery highlights the prevalence of political 
division in online news consumption and paves the way for more effective 
recommendation methods that take into account users' political views.

As discussed in the word issue thesis, current understanding of various aspects of the "word" topic is insufficient. We have identified a significant issue within the study of the word problem for the Thompson group V, which stems from an error in the presentation of V found in a previous study by Meier and Portier. Based on this flawed presentation, the paper by Meier and Portier initially concluded that a specific set of generators forms a free generating set for V, but subsequent analysis reveals that the set actually defines the free monoid on three generators, indicating that the free nature of the V growth is at best polynomial. Furthermore, the presentation in the previous study can be used to construct a group with exponential growth that is isomorphic to V, implying that several findings regarding the growth of V are either incorrect or require re-evaluation. Given the complexity of the structure of V, it is possible that a more intractable subgroup exists within V that also exhibits exponential growth.

The dynamic behavior of quantum systems under the influence of time-varying drive is highly relevant in both theoretical quantum physics and quantum technology applications. In this study, we experimentally created a quantum dot quantum spin ensemble that exhibits a periodically driven non-equilibrium steady state, and obtained key system characteristics such as densities and chemical potentials as functions of time. We further developed a theoretical model based on time-dependent rate equations to describe the quantum bit dynamics and successfully matched the experimental results. This successful match validates our developed theoretical model.

This research examines biharmonic hypersurfaces that utilize two commuting shape operators in a Euclidean space. We provide multiple new examples of biharmonic hypersurfaces categorized by their W-curvature and also demonstrate that local biharmonic hypersurfaces with specific repulsive operators, R_1 and R_2, are actually harmonic in a Euclidean space if and only if another operator, R_3, is also present.

Given positive integers p and q that share no common factors, a set of rational numbers is considered p/q-identifiable if it can be uniquely determined by the reduced residue system of integers modulo p, where each element, when divided by an integer from the set, yields a remainder of r, with r being reduced to its lowest terms. This concept is an extension of previous p-identifiable sets, which were originally defined using binary representations and later expanded to p-ary representations. The study of p/q-identifiable sets is linked to shift of deterministic automata and we explore various aspects of these sets, including their representation with base-p fractions and binary representations, and their closure under specific operations, and a relevant application is discussed.

If the active neutrino family is augmented by several sterile neutrinos with a small mass difference, a new phenomenon called the neutrino swing comes into play. The swing implies that the outcome of neutrino oscillations is heavily influenced by whether neutrinos are considered neutrinos or anti-neutrinos. The scale of this influence is primarily determined by the difference in mass and can be altered to the range of neutrino masses. The phenomenon of the swing gives rise to a new phenomenon known as the shadow substance, in which the neutrino interaction with ordinary matter results in the conversion of neutrinos into almost any other particle. The shadow substance is the product of squared conversions and thus is most pronounced for particles that are difficult to achieve. The conversion of neutrinos into anti-neutrinos during the interaction with matter becomes the dominant process. As such, the axis, which is a theoretical particle that has an extremely strong coupling with ordinary matter, can be produced in abundant quantities from the axis-induced conversion of neutrinos into axisons. The production of axisons can be compared to the production of the Sun's energy, in which axison emission can exceed other forms of loss, including neutrino emission. The results of our analysis show that if the number of sterile neutrinos is seven or more, the model, in which axison emission balances the neutrino energy, places a constraint on the mass of the axis, which is in the range of micro-electron volts. The LAMOST time-domain exploration (TDE) survey will examine four primary areas of the sky, tracked by the $K2$ mission, over a two-year span.  The data collected by LAMOST will complement the $K2$ spectra, which are limited to a single wavelength.  The radial distance and mass of stars can be determined accurately through the analysis of line-based spectra.  The $LAMOST$ spectra also provide crucial information about a star's surface composition, which cannot be obtained from radial distance alone.  The line-based spectra of $K2$ can be affected by rotational effects, which can be used to estimate a star's rotation rate.  The analysis of covariance between consecutive spectra can be used to identify transient events that cannot be detected through radial distance estimation.  The line-based and cross-dispersed $LAMOST$ spectra provide unique insights into transient variables, which can be detected at higher magnitudes than with other telescopes.  The combination of line-based and cross-dispersed spectra can be used to detect supernovae events that cannot be detected through radial distance estimation.  The analysis of transient events can be used to identify suitable targets for time-domain astronomy studies.  The features of LAMOST that can be used for time-domain studies are discussed, along with the anticipated scientific breakthroughs that can be achieved through the combination of LAMOST and other telescopes.

This paper introduces the concept of "edge-gating" in 3D semantic segmentation, 
utilizing a Edge-Gated CNN architecture that effectively combines the precision of 
edge-based methods with the efficiency of mass-based methods. By incorporating an 
edge module into a primary encoder-decoder, the model generates an edge map from a
high-resolution input, which is then fused with the primary features to produce a
highly accurate semantic segmentation. The proposed method achieves superior 
performance on two public datasets, MedSeg3D and Heart Atlas, in cardiac 
segmentation tasks, and is also made available on the open-source platform 
OpenMined.

MongoDB is a popular, document-oriented, enterprise-grade, NoSQL database that uses an ACID-compliant transactional system. Unlike traditional relational databases, it doesn't base its transactions on SQL queries, but on "2-phase commit" across document locations. However, there's no prior research on formally specifying and validating transactional integrity in MongoDB. This paper presents the first transactional correctness profile for the database, and uses Coq to verify the correctness of its document-oriented theory. We also present a transactional correctness proof and validate our framework's applicability and efficiency by formally verifying key properties of a prior proposed system.

We demonstrate $e$-positivity for the chromatic symmetric polynomials of various graph classes,
including tree-admissible graphs, and the inverse Kostka matrix is $e$-nonnegative.
This result establishes the $e$-positivity of the normalized chromatic symmetric polynomials
for all graphs as a corollary.

Hindsight summarization can retrain agents by reapplying past rewards after a history of actions, reinterpreting the value of earlier decisions based on later actions and rewards. To investigate if a Hindsight summarization approach can retrain perceivers to view actions and receive rewards similarly to a Terror Game, we applied it to the Tumor Game dataset. We found that, unlike in a Terror Game where the player is forced to take on a suboptimal strategy, the Hindsight summarization can retrain the observer to discern the optimal strategy from a suboptimal one.

Deep learning techniques have been effective in diagnosing various conditions by analyzing medical images. Nonetheless, there is a risk of bias in these images, which may stem from the training data and can lead to incorrect results. While researchers have explored bias detection and mitigation strategies for general image diagnoses, the unique characteristics of medical images necessitate a tailored approach. This paper presents a comprehensive bias framework encompassing preprocessing, processing, and post-processing stages, which can be applied to any medical image collection to identify and quantify inherent biases present in any target class. Applying this framework to lung nodule malignancy classification, we identified significant differences in bias patterns across male and female patients and observed that nodule size influenced malignancy classification accuracy in a non-linear manner. Furthermore, we propose an innovative approach to incorporate prior knowledge about inherent bias into the loss function, which can assist in reducing the impact of bias and producing more reliable medical AI systems.

Complex systems composed of interconnected components are ubiquitous in both nature and human-made environments, underpinning critical phenomena from the spread of diseases and opinions to fluctuations in financial markets and shifts in tribal cultures. A key aspect of these intricate systems lies in their concealed underlying structure and dynamics, which can be explored through concealed geometry models. A notable example of such a model is found in triangular-based assemblies of nanoscale magnetic components, often used in next-generation high-density data storage devices. By examining how magnetization shifts in response to external influences in these assemblies with triangular connections, it becomes evident that external pressure can trigger a reconfiguration of the underlying structure, analogous to a cultural renaissance, leading to altered patterns of interaction and ensuing dynamics.

On September 13, 2019, the first close approach of the Parker Solar Probe to the Sun brought about an exceptional opportunity to study the inner solar system's magnetic field and plasma conditions. Three Mini-TIPER sensors, which are sensitive to the direction of solar breeze flow, recorded three remarkable instances of the solar breeze moving in the same direction as the surrounding magnetic field. These observations were made at 0.31 and 0.33 astronomical units from the Sun, and revealed the presence of small-scale structures within the solar breeze's magnetic field. Furthermore, Mini-TIPER sensors recorded the sudden reversal of the magnetic field and a change in the solar breeze's density, temperature, and temperature, which are indicative of the collision of two opposing solar breeze waves.

Speech-emotion recognition is a deep learning-based technique that falls under the category of affect computing and is trained with labeled data to classify the emotions contained in speech. One significant challenge in this process is the discrepancy between lab-recorded data and real-life conversations, which can lead to poor speech quality and a lower accuracy of emotion detection. To address this issue, a new approach combining domain adaptation and deep reinforcement learning has been proposed. This method adapts learning across different datasets and rewards the speech-emotion recognition system with a reliability metric, thereby improving its performance in real-life situations. A U-shaped network is employed to recognize emotions and adapt its domain knowledge, which is integrated with a multi-channel system to assess the reliability of the emotions. Experimental results demonstrate the method's superiority over conventional methods and a analysis of the speech and the emotions is provided. Furthermore, a visualization of the adaptive process is explored to uncover the underlying mechanisms of the approach.

This paper investigates the effects of high pressure on the magnetic properties of a four-layer Aurivillius bi-ferrite Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ using nuclear forward scattering, from 0.01 to 10 GPa.  At normal atmospheric pressure, this material exhibits weak antiferromagnetism, but high pressure induces an abrupt transition into a state of long-range ferromagnetic order around 4.0 GPa.  In contrast, neutron diffraction data indicates the onset of long-range ferromagnetic order at higher critical pressure of approximately 7.0 GPa.  Our results are compared with existing literature to better understand the pressure-induced changes in the magnetic properties of this material.

The primary objective of the discrete-continuous shortest path problem lies in solving a hybrid version of the shortest path problem in networks, often used to optimize free-flight routes in aviation. Recent advancements in the continuous shortest path problem have utilized analytical methods to optimize a route based on a two-dimensional vector field representing air currents, particularly on a scale of 100 meters. The algorithm produces an ideal flight plan within a few seconds. In order to apply this ideal solution to real-world scenarios, it is necessary to account for the variability in air currents on a smaller scale. The algorithm can be adjusted to incorporate the uncertainty in air currents and provides a level of confidence in the optimal distance, even in the face of this uncertainty.

Researchers have extensively studied the effects of intense supernova explosions on the surrounding interstellar medium, particularly in scenarios where the shockwave encounters various states of the medium and generates complex structures. In a study, an analytical model was created to model the early dynamics of a spherical explosion occurring in a cosmologically expanding universe, taking into account the interaction of the shockwave with the interstellar medium. The model considered the early, self-similar phase of the explosion, during which the radius of the shockwave was proportional to the size of the universe, and a matched-asymptotic expansion was used to analyze the surrounding universe. However, a limitation of the existing universe description near the interface of the shockwave was the inability to account for the intense velocities generated by the explosion. A new family of self-similar inner velocity fields for the region behind the shockwave was introduced, in accordance with the laws of cosmological expansion, in order to better understand the effects of the explosion on the surrounding universe. The results of the study were verified through direct numerical simulations of the interacting shockwave and universe, in addition to the study considering the effects of the interstellar medium accumulating at the inner boundary of the explosion. The findings of the study may have relevance to the long-term dynamics of various astronomical phenomena, such as the Einstein-Crossing Phase of the Type-Ia Supernova Explosion.

Using data from LHCb, the differential decay rate of $B_s^0 \to D_s^{*-} \mu^+ \nu_{\mu}$ was studied to check the impact of accounting for the $D_s^{-} \to D_s^{-} \gamma$ decay mode's inefficiency at various points in the trajectory. A fit was performed to determine the transverse and longitudinal scattering cross-sections, and an analysis of the likelihood function's behavior was conducted to assess the shape of the decay rate. The analysis is based on 3.0 fb of lhc collision data recorded in 2015.

In this study, we create generalized Hermite polynomials, denoted as $\tilde{H}_{n,m}(x)$, which are solutions to a specific differential equation. These polynomials are connected to the Schrödinger equation through the use of identical potentials, where the energy levels depend on two variables. The requirement that the energy levels form a "Schwinger curve" is found to be closely related to the monodromy property of the associated differential equation. The polynomial solutions obtained are expressible as linear combinations of generalized Hermite polynomials, denoted as $\tilde{H}_{n,m}(x)$. The generalized Hermite polynomials are found to be orthogonal with respect to a specific weight function, a property proven through the use of a differential operator. The monodromy-free condition of the Schrödinger equation is found to be equivalent to the orthogonality of the $\tilde{H}_{n,m}(x)$ with a specific density. The $\tilde{H}_{n,m}(x)$ are shown to include ordinary Hermite polynomials as a special case. The relationship between the $\tilde{H}_{n,m}(x)$ and the ordinary generalized Hermite polynomials is explored, where the latter possess delta-function densities.

Adhesive tape removal surfaces produces a distinctive high-pitched noise known as unpeeling sound.  Research into this noise has used various models, with some classifying the source using a circular unpeeling geometry.  A novel, linear unpeeling geometry has also been explored and the geometry's impact on noise characteristics has been analyzed through both simulation and experimentation.  Findings indicate that linear unpeeling generates more consistent sound due to the directionality of the unpeeling process, and that this geometry can provide better data quality for analyzing the adhesive properties, with this approach now used in the development of an instrument called the Tape Peeler.

Time-dependent theory of planar Josephson junctions and single SQUIDs has been 
analyzed using various mathematical tools, including the Fokker-Planck equation, 
Laurent series expansions, and numerical simulations to understand the complex 
behavior of these systems. 

Our findings indicate that in certain situations, particularly when external driving 
forces are present, the conventional mean approximation is not sufficient to 
capture the intricate phase dynamics. In such cases, we found that extending the 
laplacian series to higher orders provides a more accurate representation of the 
systems' behavior. 

On the other hand, our research also shows that for unmonitored systems without 
external observation, stochastic fluctuations can lead to prolonged periods of 
apparent stability, resembling deterministic behavior. In the presence of 
external measurement, these fluctuations are suppressed, resulting in abrupt 
switching events. The systems' behavior in these scenarios can be effectively 
described by extending low-order Laplacian series. 

The research findings have significant implications for understanding the complex 
phase dynamics of planar Josephson junctions and SQUIDs, and may also inform 
similar studies of other quantum systems.

The addition of a specific combination of curling the 4-form field strength is analogous to a theta term in 5-dimensional spacetime.  Its properties mirror those of an "ether-like" interaction, and its effect becomes pronounced in hot environments, particularly in relation to the Debye temperature.  Its influence may cause the properties of charge carriers to change, thus altering their scattering, mobility, and Hall resistivity in relation to temperature, particularly in the range above this temperature threshold.  Its non-abelian variant can be incorporated into the thermodynamic properties of certain materials, including the Z2-spin liquid, anomalous Hall effect, and the Hall properties of certain metals in high temperatures.

This paper presents a method for pricing options on underlying assets subject to transaction costs arising from delta-hedging, and develops a modified delta-neutral portfolio return model accounting for the option's gamma exposure. The proposed model leads to an adjusted risk-neutral probability and a new option pricing formula, which is then applied to option collateralization through dynamic delta-hedging. The paper also includes a quantitative analysis of the impact of delta-hedging transaction costs on collateral requirements using adjusted risk-free and option-implied interest rates.

This research examines the process of approximating a complex material with varying properties as differential equations, considering differences in scale and contrast, under the constraint that high-contrast inclusions adhere to a specific framework as defined by a measure known as Hardy field. The study also analyzes a scenario where high-contrast inclusions are concentrated in a particular plane within the material. The primary findings demonstrate that the contrast and scale discrepancies can be balanced against the complex geometry of the domain, resulting in a shift from standard two-scale homogenization to a phenomenon where the effective properties are heavily influenced by the region where the inclusions are located, ultimately causing the effective material to exhibit singular behavior.

We analyzed a substantial sample of 10,514 early-type galaxies from the First and Second Data Releases of the Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam Survey using a tidal feature identification technique based on the GAIAMER method, which assesses the relative prominence of tidal tails and streams in each galaxy's profile. By assessing the proportion of galaxies with tidal features at different flux proportions, we discovered distinct characteristics between merger products and galaxies with tidal features. Mergers are typically more massive, located in the galaxy halo, and affected by higher environmental density and stellar mass density. Additionally, we determined the galaxy merger rate as a function of mass, location, and surrounding density, discovering an exponential decrease in merger rates with increasing mass and stellar mass density. Our analysis revealed a galaxy merger peak at an intermediate scale length, exceeding that of the cosmic star formation peak, highlighting the significant role of major mergers in shaping quiescent galaxies at the periphery of the $L_*$ peak.

Research in inequality focuses on opportunities, as income inequality stems from unequal opportunities and the compounding effect of advantage across generations. However, most studies overlook how opportunities change over time. This paper examines a model where individuals compete for limited positions in the same profession and create new ones in different fields. It demonstrates that in this dynamic scenario, generating new opportunities enhances social welfare and leads to greater diversity, though it may slightly decrease intergenerational mobility. Consequently, every increase in diversity brings about a net improvement in social welfare.

Effective management of high-power lasers demands innovative solutions to tackle emerging high-power laser technologies.  This paper presents a new design methodology for high-power laser systems, employing readily available commercial components.  A distinct approach is P-synchronization, a technique that enables precise temporal control of high-power lasers.  Another key development is the creation of the all-normal-dispersion mode-locked laser, which produces high-power, broad-spectrum pulses ideal for various advanced applications.  These developments have been integrated into the high-power laser laboratory at IISER Pune, resulting in several novel high-power laser systems.  In an unexpected discovery, this laboratory found that recently released declassified high-power laser technologies from the U.S. possess a design methodology remarkably similar to that of the new approach presented in this study.

We prove a novel dimension decrease property of incompressible sets in $\ell_p$ spaces. Specifically, for any incompressible set $K$ within $\ell_p$, there is a bounded metric space $F$ such that for any $\delta > 0$, an $\varepsilon$-isometric mapping from $K$ to $f_\varepsilon (K)$ exists, with $\varepsilon$ depending only on $\delta$ and $f_\varepsilon (K)$ admitting an isometric embedding into $\ell_p$ that is within $\delta$ distance of being a $\delta$-homotopy contraction.

A new method called brightness scans has been developed to characterize a beam, which is now being used in an experimental setup to extract key information about the beam in both transverse and longitudinal directions simultaneously. These characteristics include the actual stellar brightness distribution, overall star dimensions, and the actual star phase. The proposed method combines elements from traditional spatial and Fourier-based scanning techniques, and demonstrates the ability to achieve beam characterization using a single scanning device. The validity of the brightness scan technique has been confirmed through a successful test, and its advantages over conventional methods have been shown, including the potential to reduce the complexity of beam characterization while minimizing the number of required measurements.

This paper presents a distributed optimization algorithm that is resilient to malicious attacks in a network environment. The algorithm incorporates quantized updates to reduce communication overhead between agents and can be Qt-SPARTIA, the quantized and distributed version of the SPARTIA algorithm. By integrating an anti-winner-take-all filter with the gradient update, Qt-SPARTIA prevents malicious agents from dominating the system. Although Qt-SPARTIA converges at an O(1/k) rate, persistent malicious agents can influence the optimal solution. Conditions under which convergence is possible are established, and numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.

The precise measurement of the reionization peak in the Cosmic Microwave Background power spectrum is crucial for understanding early universe phenomena. However, its narrow width makes it highly susceptible to contamination from foreground errors. To address this, an accurate modeling of instrument noise patterns is essential. We have created an open-source code called s4cmb to model instrument systematic errors, which can be integrated into the simulation of intensity maps and derived spectra or power spectra. This tool is particularly useful for researchers developing and testing new analysis techniques for the data from upcoming experiments like the Reionization Observation with the Simons Array. By supplementing existing data simulations with information about the instrument's sensitivity, s4cmb enables a more realistic exploration of how foreground contamination affects the observations.

Although the excellence of prior language models in various linguistic tasks has been established, their internal mechanisms and benefits remain unclear. This study focuses on a specific aspect of these models, examining how they process individual words and word combinations. It is proposed that prior language models serve two functions: first, they help the downstream task by providing a comprehensive word representation that accounts for surrounding context; second, it is hypothesized that they also preserve a ranking of all possible word orderings, thereby maintaining a structured organization of the language space. This finding is supported by controlled experiments conducted on BART, a prominent prior language model. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the proposed focus on individual element representations and structural preservation can be utilized to develop more effective training approaches for transformer-based models.

Recently, the widespread use of deepfakes has posed significant threats in various areas, prompting extensive research into their detection. Prior work has established that effective classifiers can achieve satisfactory deepfake detection performance. However, these methods often struggle with generalization across different generators and require a vast amount of labeled data for training. In this research, we introduce a novel, unsupervised cross-sewn network called MD-CSDNetwork for deepfake detection, which excels in generalization capabilities. This model incorporates two primary components: an image feature extractor and a bidirectional detection module. By employing pre-trained image feature extractors, our framework can efficiently capture distinctive deepfake features without necessitating extensive training. The bidirectional detection module, consisting of two detection networks, is designed to identify deepfake forgeries by analyzing both original and manipulated image features. Trained on a small dataset, this module is capable of accurate detection across a wide range of other networks. Our proposed MD-CSDNetwork demonstrates remarkable performance in both supervised and unsupervised settings, achieving outstanding results on multiple public datasets in supervised settings and significantly outperforming the baseline in unsupervised settings.

Analyzing the structure of random degree-degree correlated (DDC) LDPC code graphs, this paper focuses on characterizing these graphs using the property of being -mixing. Random DDC LDPC code graphs are determined to be low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes that successfully decode over a binary erasure channel (BECh).

A novel, efficient method has been proposed to mitigate the complexity of quantum key distribution systems' vulnerability to hacking, known as the phase randomization hack. This new technique partially applies the method to the signal states, simplifying the requirement for users to implement quantum optical techniques to achieve secure communication. However, analysis shows that even with partial randomization of phases, the proposed attack can still function, yet with reduced attack speed when applied to the decoy states employed in the Li protocol hack.

This paper outlines key concepts for a self-managing and eco-friendly 5G cellular network, drawing on current research in this area. We will delve into the intricacies of a distributed control system, enabling network components to make local decisions, in contrast to a traditional central management approach. Moreover, we will examine methods for optimizing network energy consumption, a critical aspect of modern cellular networks, by leveraging energy-efficient 24x7 operation. The concept of multi-timescale network functionality is also explored.

In the 1920s, R. Menger made significant contributions to the abstract concept of angle spaces, although his work was largely overlooked. The present author's research builds upon his earlier findings from the 1920s and 1930s, which were presented at international mathematical conferences. The current study fulfills two specific axioms that had been proposed by Menger, related to the comparison of angles within space. Furthermore, the research results indicate that when the angle function is finite in a given setting, the underlying space exhibits the properties of a Hilbert space. Additionally, the author's work expands upon Menger's insights by establishing that the angle function need not be finite, provided the angle values adhere to specific criteria within an extended number system. Under these conditions, the underlying space is equivalent to a normed version of a Chebyshev space.

This article explores the connection between the efficiency of successive minimum ranking schemes in a number field K and the endomorphism ring of an elliptic curve defined over K. The bound we establish for the ratio of successive minima in such schemes is relevant to curves whose endomorphism ring is isomorphic to the integer ring of K, where our bound matches the known value of the Minkowski unit in K. This relationship aligns with an existing analogy between number fields and algebraic curves first proposed by Drinfeld. Our research confirms that the existing solution to the Mumford conjecture for genus g greater than 1 satisfies the same inequality. Additionally, our derived bound for geometrically connected curves is significantly tighter, requiring only a straightforward condition on the ring of functions without modulo genus.

A novel ultrafast rotational coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy technique has been developed in this study, allowing for the simultaneous measurement of multiple gases using a single laser system. By integrating the technique into a dual-sensor setup, researchers were able to measure the rates at which different gases rotate at vastly different time scales. The study demonstrates the ability to perform a hybrid measurement covering a wide spectrum in a single laser shot, and introduces a new data calibration algorithm to account for the wide dynamic range of data being measured. The result is the development of an algorithm capable of simultaneously measuring temperature, pressure, and individual gas concentrations in a single experiment, and is shown to have a high level of accuracy. Furthermore, this study paves the way for the measurement of multiple gases in a single experiment, and introduces the possibility of using a single laser system to measure a wide range of time scales at which different physical phenomena occur.

The formation of planets within disks surrounding young stars still relies on a
theoretical framework. Observations of young stellar disks are being made with
ever-increasing clarity thanks to advanced near-infrared telescopes, and as a
consequence, our planet formation models must be thoroughly tested. We used
a simplified model of disk evolution to see how the flow of material within the
disk is connected to the development of planets. This SSED model connects the
amount of material accreted by the star with the location of solid material
accumulation in the disk. Findings show that where dust turns into rock in the
disk affects the amount of material available for making planetary cores. It also
indicates that the amount of material in the inner disk is influenced by the
viscosity caused by magnetic fields. Additionally, it appears that the amount of
gas in the outer disk is affected by dust accumulation, and it may help explain
why some exoplanets are rich in heavy elements.

Recent observations from the CERN Large Hadron Collider's Run 1 indicate that neutral patterns in the forward regions of the detector may have an impact on performance and create neutral areas. A simulation was conducted to assess the effect of these patterns on a vacuum chamber in a linear setup, using both neutral and stripe-like neutral fields. Results show that neutral patterns can significantly reduce the直流 current produced on the downstream chamber in an estimated $10^{-12}$ Ampere scale. In contrast, stripe-like neutral patterns have a much smaller estimated effect of around $10^{-13}$ Ampere. If LHC's superconducting dipole magnets experience similar neutral patterns, they could have a beneficial impact on the performance of the machine.

We introduce two distinct U_q(g) - cluster structures for any Kac-Moody algebra g, 
establishing their connection via braid group action when g is a finite type algebra. 
These structures enable us to express the quantum group as a cluster skew group ring, 
specifically in the case of gl(n). This approach yields a cluster monomial basis for the positive 
part of the quantum group and facilitates a cluster expression for the crystal base or the 
Kashiwara polynomial basis of the U_q(g)-module V_l.

This research introduces a novel decentralized teaching learning algorithm, which we call DR-DSGD, that incorporates distributional robustness into the decentralized setting. DR-DSGD enhances the standard teaching learning process by equipping the agent with the ability to withstand adversarial corruption of data. Specifically, we expand the data teaching complexity from O(d^2 log log (1/epsilon)) to the distributed setting with a consideration of graph connectivity. We can see from the results of simulation experiments that a teaching sample size of roughly 20 per dimension is required to achieve high accuracy in a decentralized environment using the DR-DSGD algorithm. Furthermore, our results show that a data teacher can significantly decrease the number of communication rounds between learners by a factor of d among k learners.

We examine current computer simulation methodologies for 'hard-driven' systems, comparing them to older methods and highlighting common approaches adopted by researchers. Current research has been significantly impacted by limited access to computationally efficient approaches due to widespread adoption of Exascale computing. We contrast 'microscopically realistic' simulations with 'coarse-grained' models, discussing how each deals with storage density and heat transfer. Furthermore, we discuss the influence of drive architecture and file system on simulated performance. We categorize simulation approaches based on their focus: system, media, or drive, and explore how each approach addresses key factors such as heat transfer, mechanical limitations, data storage density, and read/write head effects.

This paper investigates jet generation within a medium using PYTHIA 6.25 and EPOS3, utilizing realistic initial conditions from CGC-based proton and neutron PDFs. By simulating central Pb-Pb and p-p collisions at various energy levels, we assess the impact of initial conditions and PDF scale on jet characteristics. Our analysis reveals the persistence of medium-modified jet suppression even after accounting for initial conditions, with additional jet energy loss gained through 4-momenta re-sampling. Notably, energy loss reduction amounts to about 10-15 GeV in Wpp and roughly 20-25 GeV in Pbpb. Furthermore, increased initial energy leads to increased final energy, impacting the interpretation of jet data in terms of medium properties. Establishing the relationship between jet energy and energy lost to the medium requires considering nuclear effects and their dependence on collision system and centrality. Sensitivity to initial conditions also influences observables like elliptic flow and azimuthal anisotropies, with modified directed and elliptic flow re-sampled to match pp data, and modified Rcp re-sampled to match p-p data in specific centrality ranges. Modified retension derived from medium energy and temperature re-sampled to match p-p data, showing only slight differences in lead-proton, proton-proton, and proton-proton collisions. We conclude that energy scale effects significantly influence medium properties derived from jet data, impacting the extraction of temperature and tension from jet

The cryptocurrency sector has been the focus of numerous scams in recent years,
with pyramid schemes being among them. These schemes often employ complex
blockchain technology and user-friendly interfaces to deceive victims into believing
they are making a sound investment. One particularly large pyramid scheme, Forsage,
originated in 2018 with earnings claims that seemed too good to be true. Forsage's
profitability was heavily dependent on recruiting new members, with the company's
earnings dashboard providing little information about the actual value of their
digital assets. As of 2020, Forsage contracts were worth virtually nothing in terms
of cryptocurrency value, with the company's financial model relying on a classic
pyramid scheme structure. This paper aims to shed light on the inner workings of
pyramid schemes through an in-depth analysis of Forsage, with the hope of educating
potential victims and preventing future scams.

The VISTA Variable Star Survey (VVV) has been used to identify 19 new globular clusters in the Milky Way's bulge region. The VVV team conducted a comprehensive examination of the VVV data in the $J$,$K_S$ color-magnitude space, resulting in the discovery of these additional clusters, which join a previously known group of 46 in this area. The clusters were given individual parameters, such as distance modulus, metallicity, and extinction values. They were further classified into one normal cluster and 18 anomalous clusters, the latter of which display atypical properties like multi-populations, tidal effects, or unusual features like torn-apart structures. The VVV catalog significantly expands upon existing lists of globular clusters in the bulge region, notably due to VLV cluster detection capabilities. This enhanced understanding will contribute valuable information to the broader study of cluster formation history in the galaxy's central region.

This study aims to resolve the issue of large logarithmic terms appearing in certain exclusive processes, such as certain dijet production processes, which can significantly interfere with the detection of new particles beyond the Standard Model at hadron colliders. While initial attempts to regulate these logarithmic terms involved all-order cancellations between different frameworks, like Soft-Collinear Effective Theory and the factorization framework, a more straightforward method of solving this issue has been discovered. An innovative approach has been discovered to resolve the issue of large logarithmic terms in certain exclusive quark influence functions, such as those relevant for dijet production, through a combination of factorization and summation techniques. This approach involves factorizing the cross-section into distinct components and then utilizing the discrete nature of final state particles to derive a new, all-inclusive definition of the cross-section that automatically incorporates the required coherence factors. As a result, the issue of large logarithmic terms can be resolved through a more straightforward method of infinite cancellations between different components of the factorization framework. This approach can be derived through a combination of factorization arguments and numerical simulations, which have confirmed the accuracy of the results. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that the issue of large logarithmic terms can be resolved through a more straightforward method of infinite cancellations between different components of the factorization framework, which involves summing the contributions of different components of the cross-section to obtain a accurate, all-inclusive definition of the cross-section that automatically incorporates the required coherence factors.

The accuracy of first-principle calculations is guaranteed, and they are commonly used in quantum dynamics simulations based on the real-time time-dependent density functional theory. However, such simulations demand extensive computational resources, and therefore, simplified tight-binding models are often used for easier and faster computations. Although these models facilitate faster computations, the randomness of the model's parameters typically compromises the reliability of the results. We have developed a highly symmetric tight-binding model that mirrors the electronic band structure of silicon within its high-symmetry Dirac point, and we have demonstrated its utility in modeling the femtosecond charge carrier dynamics. By conducting simulations, we have shown that despite the model's high Dirac velocity being significantly lower than the values obtained from first-principle calculations, it accurately replicates the charge carrier mobility. Furthermore, our results indicate that model invariance to the on-site disorder can be achieved in high-symmetry systems, and this can lead to more computationally efficient simulations when compared to traditional disordered tight-binding models.

In this research, a new variant of the holographic multi-scale entanglement renormalization ansatz (hMERAs) is introduced, an improved version where the shadow region remains consistent across different data qubits, a characteristic known as hyperinvariance. A specific type of hyperinvariant hMERA is then developed to efficiently represent large shadow regions with limited entanglement, demonstrating strong resemblance to good holographic codes. Furthermore, it is shown that certain errors can be reliably recovered from the neural network structure, utilizing locally invertible operations within the unitary blocks. In relation to traditional invariant hMERA s, our findings suggest a potentially useful direction for representing systems with power-law decay behaviors.

A theoretical analysis of retinal's photoisomerization from a retulene model highlights the phenomenon of sensitive resonance enhancement.  By applying semi-classical rate equations with resonance-integrated coordinates and solving for steady-state values, a significant rise in the reaction rate is found near the critical frequency.  This result indicates a highly variable photoisomerization ratio in retinal and related carotenoid molecules, with the intensity of resonance sensitivity so far unobserved.  This model suggests that the visual pigment may operate near the peak of sensitive resonance to minimize noise-induced variations in the signal it processes.

In today's data-driven world, organizations are collecting vast amounts of information to enhance their business processes. With the help of Machine Learning techniques, companies can make sense of this data, make better-informed decisions and more accurate forecasts about their business processes. This study focuses on comparing several Machine Learning models, including LogBooster, Random Forest, Neural Network and XGBoost, to see which is most effective at understanding, ranking, making predictions and classifying Business Process Process Mining (BPPM) attributes. By extensively testing these models on a large dataset, this research aims to provide a comprehensive guide for practitioners in the BPPM field when selecting the right Machine Learning approach for their needs.

Social networking platforms provide invaluable resources for understanding public sentiment and enhancing crisis management strategies. Analyzing online discussions can reveal crucial insights into people's feelings and thoughts, especially during emergencies. This paper aims to examine citizens' responses and feelings following earthquakes in Turkey, with a specific focus on the Izmir seismic event of October 30, 2020. By conducting text mining analysis of posts related to the earthquake on Twitter in Turkish, we uncovered key themes reflecting a mix of fear, concern, and hope for a swift recovery and reconstruction. These findings demonstrate the utility of social media data in understanding and addressing public needs in times of crisis.

This paper delves into the non-triviality and fundamental properties of various Gelfand-Shilov areas. It also examines the non-triviality and basic characteristics of specific Toeplitz operator symbols within these areas, and implies that certain Toeplitz operators are well-defined and continuous across the Gelfand-Shilov areas.

AD Leo is a well-documented classical Cepheid variable star that has been extensively observed and modeled over the past few decades.  In contrast to other single-star supernovae, the 1985 Great Eruption of AD Leo remained unassociated with any companion star until recently.  Using newly acquired near-ultraviolet spectra from the Pegasus-2 and Pegasus-3 spectrographs, this study determined the effective temperature of AD Leo during its 1985 Great Eruption to be around 9600 K.  When compared to models from the previous two decades, this temperature is notably cooler.  By combining the new near-UV data with optical spectra from the previous study, this research developed improved expansion velocity and luminosity models for AD Leo's 1985 Great Eruption, which are 10% and 20% more precise than the earlier models.  The findings suggest that the 1985 Great Eruption of AD Leo is an event with an initial temperature of approximately 9600 K.

A theoretical analysis of PT-symmetric waveguide networks is presented, examining the impact of imaginary cross-coupling on radiation loss, the clarity of image transmission, and the relationship between CPA and lasing in finite periodic structures. Analysis shows that in isolated cross-coupled waveguide sections, maximum loss occurs at specific frequencies influenced by the sign of the imaginary coupling, whereas clear bidirectional transmission is achieved only when direct and cross-coupling parameters are balanced, happening at particular angles in obliquely connected sections. Furthermore, it is found that the interplay between coupled modes in finite periodic structures with PT-symmetry determines the emergence of supermode loss and amplification, in contrast to the enhanced submode behaviors in symmetric configurations. These theoretical insights provide a path for utilizing PT-symmetric finite periodic structures in applications requiring controlled energy dissipation and enhanced sensitivity.

The analysis of large-scale networks is complicated by limited data availability, which often makes it challenging to apply traditional reduction techniques effectively. As an alternative, we explored the dynamics of sparse logical networks that can incorporate both multi-node interactions and self-interactions. We observed that these networks exhibit dynamics that are consistent with empirical data from biological networks, in contrast to the dynamics predicted by standard BA models. Notably, we found that an essential feature of the network's topological structure, rather than a specific topological characteristic, dictates the overall dynamics. We developed a generalised sLL model that exhibits dynamics aligned with those of biological networks.

The structural analysis of atomic nuclei relies heavily on the Holstein-Hartree-Bogoliubov (HHHB) method, and its success heavily depends on accurately computing matrix elements of one-body and two-body operators between HHB states. This paper derives the general formulas for the matrix elements of one-body and two-body operators between arbitrary HHB configurations, using the information about the HHB wave function obtained from the HHB equations. Furthermore, we demonstrate our formulas' effectiveness by calculating matrix elements in the HHB configurations constructed from HHB single-quasiparticle states within the GCM-HHB framework.

This paper introduces a novel technique for point cloud denoising and reconstruction,
called the 'Transformation-Unique Smoothing' (TUS) framework. Unlike previous
methods that utilized point-based loss functions, TUS transforms point clouds into
binary masks via cross-sectional slices, enabling the application of well-established
image processing techniques for mask refinement. By integrating a flexible
transformation-based loss function, our method achieves precise point cloud
smoothing and structure recovery. The proposed TUS framework is further explained
in our unique strategy for point cloud processing, called 'Transformation-Unique
Smoothing'.

We investigate two medium access methods, ALOHA and CSMA, for low-frequency radio (LFR) and continuous wave (FMCW) combined technology in smart home settings.  Due to the absence of physical layer signaling in FMCW, higher layer protocols are necessary, which we propose assesses the merits of CSMA through simulations using real-world data. Our analysis involves examining various FMCW operating parameters, ALOHA slot durations, and FMCW ramp durations to ALOHA slot ratio, ultimately yielding an optimal configuration for the latter. Next, we test the ALOHA and CSMA techniques with actual FMCW-based LFR devices, using IBM Real Time Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (RFMCW) hardware, and evaluate their performance via a benchmark based on the well-established 802.15.4 protocol, which incorporates FMCW for improved range, in an F2M-CR context. Our results show CSMA outperforms ALOHA and the CSMA binary exponential backoff variant in specific test scenarios, also providing criteria for successful implementation and setting a comparative standard against 802.15.4 using actual hardware.

Temporal knowledge graph completion focuses on predicting unknown connections in a time-based knowledge graph. A vast number of prediction methods exist, yet a unifying theory explaining their comparable performance does not. This research evaluates a range of popular and lesser-known approaches and conducts thorough experiments to give each a fair assessment. A comprehensive benchmark and over 5000 testing scenarios are established to assess various methods under consistent conditions. Our analysis reveals that graph completion can be effectively solved by grouping representations into two categories: model-dependent and model-independent. Both categories outperform individual approaches. Notably, two previously underappreciated baseline methods are found to be among the most effective in their respective categories.

Within the RPA framework, Jost functions are constructed using the Skyrme force, and two complex eigenenergies of the isoscalar dipole resonance in $^{16}$O are reported.

The use of Jost functions in describing scattering and bound states provides a link to scattering data, and analyzing the RPA polynomial's roots for eigenenergies may be substituted with evaluating the RBA Jost functions.

The existence of the GDR in $^{16}$O' s spectrum is currently unexplained by the RBA using Skyrme forces, and further study is needed.

Identifying groups of similar systems from a large number of trajectories is a crucial step in applying machine learning techniques to stabilize and optimize multiple similar systems simultaneously. Existing methods usually require pre-knowledge about the systems' underlying structure and often struggle with precision and computation time when applied to a large number of trajectories. This paper proposes a novel, trajectory-driven approach that groups systems together by evaluating how much one system's data influences another, requiring only flat programming and little computation time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method by successfully clustering multiple similar systems, namely a pair of pendulums and a set of double pendulums with comparable swing patterns.

Text generation using neural networks is currently dominated by large-scale deep learning models, particularly those based on the Transformer architecture with numerous parameters. While the success of such models is undeniable, using them as a baseline for new approaches is compromised due to the high computational cost of comparing their performance against. In contrast to existing methods that evaluate against the massive BERT model, our proposed framework, SparseGAN, contrasts a smaller, more efficient generator with a simpler discriminator. Our framework diverges from traditional Generative Adversarial Networks in that it trains the generator and discriminator antagonistically. Surprisingly, despite our models being smaller and fewer in number, our language creation model achieves performance on par with the large-scale deep learning model on several evaluation metrics. Moreover, our approach reduces training and evaluation time by a factor of 10, making it a more practical and efficient high school for text generation.

The hypothesis of interstellar panspermia suggests that life has the capacity to travel across stars, yet this idea lacks sufficient scientific evidence. Researchers are drawn to studying how life affects its environment in the extraterrestrial environments of the solar system and planetary systems, in an effort to answer questions about its durability and transportability in the cosmic environment. This effort is facilitated by combining experimental simulations with theoretical models of planetary atmospheres and the discovery of exoplanets. Current laboratory facilities capable of replicating the harsh conditions found on the solar system's small bodies and comets are now able to study these environments in detail. However, there is a limitation in observing these experiments from the outside, particularly when considering the role of solar radiation which can have a significant effect on the survival of organisms. This paper discusses the concept of interstellar panspermia and analyzes how life may endure and be transported in the solar system and on exoplanets, in order to identify any tell-tale signs of its plausibility when investigating the cosmic environment surrounding these small bodies.

We have developed a theoretical framework for interference patterns in HI intensity mapping surveys, which account for the impact of photon density waves on the survey's ability to measure the Hubble expansion and the matter power spectrum. This framework includes predictions for the interference pattern's scale dependence and the effects of removing the survey's interfering region through simulation. Furthermore, a simple mathematical model is proposed to quantify the bias and noise introduced by this process, and it is found that eliminating the interference pattern can shift the effective w-scale of the power spectrum by a significant amount, impacting the interpretation of intensity mapping data in the context of future cosmological studies.

We've developed a theoretical concept called the "spontaneous symmetry disruption chain" and applied it to the D4 model of SU(4) color symmetry, which is composed of four quarks of type A and four quarks of type B. By having the mass of the A-quark be less than that of the B-quark, the ground state of the D4 model experiences a spontaneous symmetry disruption. However, if the mass difference is reversed, the system's ground state remains in a symmetric state. Through a mechanism known as the "Higgs mechanism," the system's symmetry is broken in a chain-like fashion. Additionally, we found that four-quark states with unbroken SU(4) color symmetry can be created using the Higgs mechanism.

Combining spatial capture-recapture data with location-based survey information has been shown to significantly boost the reliability of statistical estimates for animal populations. Nonetheless, a major hurdle in studying certain species lies in their elusive nature, making live captures rare. Research on habitat and resource selection typically relies on indirect evidence, such as scat analysis or camera traps, which may not accurately reflect an animal's actual location due to their tendency to avoid detection methods. This study presents a new statistical method that incorporates SCCR data with indirect resource selection observations in their respective contexts, allowing for more accurate animal population estimates. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness using simulated data and real-world examples of grizzly cats and red deer, also offering insights into avoiding biased conclusions by carefully selecting the type of data used for resource selection.

This paper addresses minimal power $k$ edge disjoint $st$-paths in directed graphs, which involves finding the smallest integer minimal power $k$ where it is possible to identify $k$ edge disjoint $st$-paths in a directed graph by assigning a capacity of at least $k$ to each edge based on its existence.

Estimating the minimal power of directed graphs required for containing a large number of edge-disjoint $st$-paths has been a key barrier in the development of local sparsifiers and low-sketch flow algorithms. Currently, the best result for directing graphs is due to a recent algorithm by Andries, Parter, and Solomon, which provides an $O(\sqrt[4]{k})$ estimator for directed graphs.

In this study, we introduce an $O(\sqrt{k})$ estimator for directed graphs, achieving a square root dependence on the number of $st$-paths.

This paper presents an innovative approach to managing swarms of unmanned aerial vehicles that involves cognizance, a technique allowing individual vehicles to make autonomous decisions while maintaining awareness of their surroundings. Our proposed swarm control method enables each UAS to independently assess its environment and anticipate events, facilitating free flight and self-organized routing without the need for centralized command. By applying this method to several swarms simultaneously, our approach also shows improved safety through the use of limited information and localized communication networks. We demonstrate our concept using realistic simulations that show the potential for efficient, secure swarm operation.

Local connections within the networks significantly influence various processes that occur over time, with a particular focus on random walks and dynamic communities.
Researchers have devised and explored multiple models to capture the phenomenon of dynamic communities, with a particular emphasis on a novel model called Time-Dependent Random Walk (TDRW).
In this study, we have examined how a specific parameter affects TDRW by investigating both simulated and real-world network data, with a particular interest in comparing and contrasting its outcomes with those of random walks and the LTM model.
Our findings demonstrate that the TDRW model exhibits a distinct form of localization, setting it apart from the results obtained from the LTM model, while also suggesting that a higher degree of community formation emerges when nodes with a higher degree are located within smaller and more compact clusters.

This study examines geographical patterns in UEFA EURO 2020 and 2022 tournaments, focusing on the effectiveness of teams' defensive strategies. By applying GADs, a method to assess defensive capabilities, and incorporating geospatial data visualization techniques, the analysis considers the probability of players scoring goals and the influence of home fields. Key aspects explored include the impact of home field advantage, player distribution across countries, and variations in goal prevention capabilities across different age groups. The results are displayed through interactive 3D maps generated with the help of the plotly R package.

Modern automated systems heavily depend on information extraction and form interpretation, which is often complicated by the vast diversity of form designs encountered. While deep learning has excelled in structured data extraction tasks using consistent appearance, its application to forms of unlimited design variability remains a challenge. This study introduces an innovative visual template-free form interpretation approach, which combines a pre-trained autoencoder with a selective fine-tuning strategy to achieve this goal. Uniquely, our method does not require any form design templates, instance forms, or design variation annotations during training. Interestingly, it can be interpreted as a virtual side-scrolling platform game, where autoencoder layers correspond to game components and data fields are like collectible coins. Surprisingly, despite its simplicity, this approach outperforms sophisticated multi-view template matching techniques and is among the top-performing visual data extraction methods using limited training data. Additionally, our research showcases the virtually limitless applicability of this pioneering approach through a set of diverse real-world form scenarios.

This research introduces the Concealed Parameter Recurrent State Space (CoReSS) frameworks, an innovative concept that alters standard dynamical models by incorporating a concealed parameter. In CoReSS frameworks, the concealed parameter is said to modify dynamic scenarios. We express CoReSS frameworks in a general form and examine the conditions under which specific transformations can be applied to the models' states to reveal the effects of the concealed parameter on dynamics. A crucial condition for the existence of a concealed parameter state transformation (CPST) is that the models belong to a class called $\mathcal{C}$ models. We derive the specific characteristics of models $\mathcal{C}$ models and demonstrate that CoReSS frameworks can be understood as combinations of two separate models $\mathcal{C}$, provided that the concealed parameter has a finite number of discrete values. We further show that certain well-known CoReSS frameworks, including Hidden Markov Models (HMMs), change their underlying states as the parameter varies. A novel, general method is also suggested to investigate the effects of the concealed parameter on dynamics, allowing it to be applied to a wide range of CoReSS frameworks.

We investigate the concept of conditional freeness of type $B$ and its connection to stochastic block models as the matrix dimension increases. 
An examination is performed on how stochastic block models relate to random matrices with given probability matrices and free or type $B$ independence.
A new concept of conditional freeness of type $B$ is defined and some basic properties are explored.
An example demonstrating the emergence of certain kinds of conditional type $B$ independence from stochastic block models is defined and some results on large $N$ limits of small adjacency matrices are investigated.
An explanation of how random matrices with given probability matrices can arise from matrices whose entries are conditionally free or type $B$ independent, given an even matrix size $N$, is investigated in the context of even traces and odd monomials, and some related questions are discussed.

For curves of genus one, we've created a family of covers of degree three over curves of genus one, and analyzed an associated Prym variety which is actually isomorphic to the original curve. This type of non-classical cover allows for an explicit derivation of the Jacobian of the covered curve as well. These findings are applied to a specific curve defined by the equation x^4 + y^4 = z^4.

The significance of structural polarization within networks is still the subject of intense debate, with multiple proposals made to quantify its impact. Nevertheless, a unified approach has yet to be established, and the comparison between various methods remains limited. This research addresses these gaps by evaluating five widely used structural polarization metrics against a novel proposal, known as the disturbance difference. Firstly, a thorough comparison between these methods is conducted to highlight their commonalities and differences. Moreover, several comparison scenarios are executed to assess their polarization sensitivity. This study's outcome provides a standardization of polarizing structures assessment that can serve as a reference point for future work in this area.

The concept of multilayer networks is pivotal in understanding multiple interacting systems. Within these phase oscillator networks, we examine the dynamics of multiple layers and how they can be reduced to a single, effective layer. We discover that certain solutions in higher-order networks can be 'transmitted' from simpler, lower-order configurations. This phenomenon of transmission allows multilayer systems of any order to be comprehended as combinations of single-layer configurations. Moreover, we identify conditions under which multilayer networks exhibit transmission of solutions from their constituent single-layer components.

A recent development in the physics of continuum mechanics has been the introduction of the Cauchy stress operator as the fundamental building block for rate-dependent continuum theories. Its ability to seamlessly derive other fields, such as the first kind's Cauchy stress tensor, Eulerian elasticity tensor, and various other elasticity tensors, makes it an invaluable tool. The objective of this research is to identify the most concise form of the Cauchy stress operator in accordance with the principles of material objectivity and the supply of symmetry conditions for the Cauchy stress tensor. Additionally, the resulting concised expressions will be applied to specific constitutive models to demonstrate their benefit in deriving complex stress-related stress rates and other stress-related quantities.

Geometric programming evaluation is a method that leverages the algebraic and graphical features of equations to provide an intuitive, visual, and user-friendly means of assessing complex relationships in a program. This approach uses simple, linear equations to map out a program's flow graph and delivers a clear, coherent view of its internal workings, ultimately making it easier to assess the program's readability, reliability, and efficiency.

We introduce HyperPrompt, an innovative architecture that utilizes HyperNetworks to create adaptable task-conditioning for self-attention within Transformers through prompt-like learnable task embeddings. This method allows for the preservation of pre-trained knowledge from frozen Transformer models, ensuring efficient utilization of available data and preventing performance degradation due to over-parameterization. HyperPrompt exhibits exceptional versatility and can be applied to a diverse range of tasks including Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, and Multi-Modality, while also exhibiting scalable results across multiple datasets and tasks in each modality. Furthermore, HyperPrompt showcases superior versatility compared to prominent multi-task alternatives, particularly in scenarios with limited data for certain tasks.

Let $\sigma$ be a symmetric positive-definite matrix of size $n^2 \times n^2$, and let $\mathbf{v}$ be a vector in the space $M_n(\mathbb{R})$. We can think of $\mathbf{v}$ as a matrix of the same size as $\sigma$. The trajectory of $\mathbf{v}$ is defined as $e^{t\sigma}\mathbf{v}e^{t\sigma^T}$ for all non-negative values of $t$. If both $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are symmetric and positive-definite matrices, the rate of exponential decay of the determinant of the trajectory of $\mathbf{v}$ is bounded above by three-quarters of the difference between the largest and smallest eigenvalues of the symmetric part of $\sigma$ and bounded below by the same value for the largest eigenvalue of $\sigma$.

This research focuses on high-brightness laser operation, spanning in the Terahertz to mid-infrared range, using a dual-gain configuration with identical quantum well structures separated by barriers that enforce symmetry. The study reveals that applying an electric field can selectively enhance emission at specific wavelengths while suppressing emission at others, due to the preservation of optical transitions' parity in accordance with the kind of bundle used. As a result, high-brightness operation can be achieved at line edges without the need for carrier capture or heavy-hole hole participation. Notably, the research demonstrates up to five-fold increased brightness in operation mode 0/1 compared to standard quantum well lasers, along with an 80 nm range in high-brightness emission.

This paper presents a network scale estimation method for a given graph, effective even when the graph is affected by a unknown number of Byzantine failures. We develop an efficient algorithm that identifies a significant subset of the graph, approximately 1/10th of its vertices, formed by neighboring relationships up to a distance of 2. This algorithm runs in a time frame of O(n^(4/3)) and allows for an alternative analysis yielding a time frame of n^(0.85) when vertex weights are considered, all while ensuring correctness with a high probability.

Accurate short-term size predictions for urban queues at intersections are crucial for effective traffic management and navigation. This document presents a novel, data-driven approach to estimating queue lengths without reliance on historical traffic patterns or predefined road network data. By utilizing the positions of probe vehicles near intersections, the proposed method projects their locations to determine individual queue lengths and total counts. This approach is flexible and adaptable, allowing it to be tailored to various road configurations and traffic scenarios. The method was tested using real-world data from three intersections in different urban areas, and the results demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy compared to previous techniques, particularly in scenarios involving multiple lanes.

New generations of numerical relativity simulations, accounting for complex phenomena and phenomena observed in gravitational waves, require a more robust handling of initial data that can accommodate a wide range of astrophysical scenarios. One notable limitation of the conventional methods is the inability to place the horizon/surface within the stellar interior, often forcing it to coincide with the horizon itself. Our proposed method overcomes this constraint by numerically determining the location of the horizon through an iterative process, allowing the horizon to be positioned anywhere inside the stellar interior. This, in turn, minimizes the thickness of the horizon/ surface layer to its physical thickness, typically measured in grid points, and reduces the spurious effects that can arise from artificial boundary conditions, such as the non-physical mass ejection that can occur when a stellar surface is set at the horizon itself. Furthermore, our method is applicable to both rotating and non-rotating black holes/stars, and can be incorporated into the popular $\Gamma$-driver shift condition to stabilize the simulation of a stellar surface behind a black hole's horizon, often resulting in the star being sucked into the black hole's interior.

The $\Sigma^+ \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$ transition, which has not yet been observed, can be extensively studied using existing data from the LHCb experiment. By utilizing the LHCb dataset from 2015 and 2016 runs at 7 TeV and 8 TeV, respectively, amounting to 3.0 inverse femtobarns and 3.0 inverse femtobarns, the first comprehensive analysis of this rare process is conducted. This study builds upon a preceding search presented in 2017 during the 41st International Symposium on on Electron and Photon Detectors, where an updated outcome is now presented.

Ultra-thin magnetic material layers can exhibit new properties due to strong quantum confinement and interaction with the substrate, making them useful for various applications.  Recent studies have highlighted the potential of combining 2D materials with 5d magnetic materials to create new phases with unique properties like large spin-orbit interaction and net magnetization.  A newly synthesized ultra-thin variant of the Heusler alloy, Mn$_3$NiN, exhibits rare properties such as antiferromagnetism and the Nernst effect.  Despite its antiferromagnetic state, the material exhibits unusually large transverse voltages generated by changing temperatures in strong perpendicular magnetic fields.  Further analysis using X-ray techniques and first-principles calculations show that an isolated Mn$_3$NiN layer is in the double perovskite structure with net ferromagnetic moments, which may be distorted into a non-collinear state by the substrate, thus facilitating the observed Nernst effect.  This research provides valuable insights into understanding the sources of the effect and suggests that this material could be a promising candidate for studying complex electronic behaviors in ultra-thin layers.

Recently, automatic label generation by strong models has been successfully applied and is now considered a promising approach for creating high-quality datasets for training strong recognition systems. This concept forms the basis for the development of self-supervised learning methods and self-trained systems. Nonetheless, when multiple teacher models are involved, the quality of the generated labels can be compromised due to the potential for label conflicts. To tackle this problem, we introduce Pairwise Iterative Logits Aggregation for multi-teacher labeled distillation (PILE), an innovative framework consisting of two primary components. Initially, we establish pairwise relationships between model pairs to generate reliable dataset labels. Subsequently, through an iterative label fusion process guided by a student network, the generated labels are combined into high-quality labels that effectively capture the multi-teacher information. As a result, PILE enables the generation of superior data from multiple teacher models and yields enhanced performance in downstream evaluation. Empirical evidence from extensive experiments on the MS-COCO dataset demonstrates the superiority of PILE over alternative single-teacher learning strategies and carefully designed baseline methods, resulting in state-of-the-art outcomes.

Accelerator physics primarily relies on describing particle motion using "ray" trajectories in a classical mechanics framework, with the "ray" representing the path of whole particles. In a circular accelerator, these rays are analyzed in both spatial and temporal dimensions to study dynamics in phase space. A key aspect of this analysis is the relationship between ray and particle motion, which is examined through the concept of beta functions that describe the amplitude of oscillatory motion. Understanding these beta functions is crucial in assessing beam losses caused by various imperfections in the accelerator. Furthermore, an essential requirement in the design of accelerator components is that they be "laminar", meaning they allow ray trajectories to remain confined within a certain range without permitting particles to hit the walls of the device.

The user centers around the world are pivotal in providing essential resources for research users, including computing facilities, research tools, and data sets. To optimize these resources, user centers employ a range of sophisticated software systems that facilitate complex software, data sets, and remote instruments. However, to minimize downtime and optimize the efficiency of these resources, it is crucial to quickly diagnose and rectify any issues that may arise. In fact, the daily occurrence of unexpected system failures at user centers makes this crucial. To address this issue, machine learning is emerging as a game-changing technology for the user centers around the world. Its ability to process information at an unprecedented speed and scale makes it an ideal solution. This paper explores the transformative potential of machine learning in the user centers around the world, focusing on the speed and accuracy of machine learning in diagnosing issues, the development of automated software systems that can operate without human intervention, and the use of machine learning in the interpretation of scientific data. This discussion is focused on the user centers around the world and is expected to be of interest to researchers in the fields of computer science, electrical engineering, and related disciplines.

This paper builds on recent work in differential analysis, addressing limitations of prior studies that focused mainly on autonomous systems.
