The proposed discrete approximations for the fractional Laplacian operator Λ^s f(x) can be simplified to involve the standard discrete Laplacian operator Δ. For a broad category of complete, non-compact metric measure spaces with a compact boundary, we demonstrate that certain discrete porous medium type equations converge in the limit as the approximation parameter tends to 1 to the continuous fractional porous medium type equations. These approximations are based on the standard discrete Laplacian operator Δ. The limit case of approximation for the fractional porous medium type equations can be simplified to involve the standard discrete Laplacian operator Δ.

We delve into the foundational aspects of mathematics, focusing on Godel's incompleteness theorems, which are considered primary limitations of classical first-order logic. Notably, Godel's second incompleteness theorem establishes that the consistency of basic mathematics cannot be proven by the mathematics itself. A crucial component of this theorem is the ability to translate mathematical statements back and forth within the same logical system. However, this translation technique can be utilized to demonstrate that if certain statements are true, then the logical system can also prove its own consistency. Using this approach, Godel was able to create an alternative statement with equivalent meaning to the original, thereby proving that the system is either incomplete or susceptible to alternative interpretations. This same reasoning can be employed to make similar assertions about other complex propositions, such as those related to set theory.

In Clifford analysis, an operator T analogous to the Cauchy-Riemann operator from complex analysis has dirac operator $\gamma_\mu \partial_\mu$ as its primary form in physics. From this, a representation theory for the Poincaré group can be obtained. We utilize the eigenfunctions of the Dirac operator, $\varphi_k$, in a compact domain D to represent any smooth function f in D through an integral involving a kernel, $\sigma$, which is also an eigenfunction of the Dirac operator. By expanding $\sigma$ in a basis of eigenfunctions, its expansion coefficients are found to be constant, independent of position in D. We integrate these coefficients against $\varphi_k$ in D to obtain a new kernel, $K_k$, whose values at the boundary of D are used to represent any smooth function in D through an integral involving a function g in D. An analysis of $K_k$ in R^3 reveals that it satisfies the three-spheres identity, where its values at two constant radii, r and R, in D are equal to an integral involving g at all radii, r', in D.

This paper introduces a novel approach called Sequential Geographically Balanced Sampling (SeGBS) to balance cost and accuracy when making balanced selections from points scattered across a continuous area. Traditionally, Geographically Balanced Sampling (GBS) has been used for accurate balanced selections, but it demands geocoding and can become costly when working with continuous domains. To address this challenge, we propose SeGBS, a method that gradually samples a two-dimensional domain and introduces a new efficiency metric for evaluating its performance. By using a geometric probability approach, we geocode points and sample them in a geographically balanced sequence. A case study comparing SeGBS and GBS on the U.S. demonstrates the former's cost advantages while maintaining comparable accuracy.

Robotic systems that use eye-to-hand cameras are essential for performing real-time image analysis and manipulating objects.  However, the precise alignment of these cameras is often affected by slight inaccuracies in calibration due to the nature of the used semi-flexible lenses.  As a result, obtaining an accurate camera internal parameter set becomes a significant challenge.  Current methods of calibration are usually costly and require the assistance of human operators to manually adjust the lens or employ expensive external equipment to measure the flexible lens parameters.  In this research, a novel approach to calibration is proposed that relies on a unique eye-to-hand dataset, in which a human operator places an object within view of the camera and adjusts the camera's position and orientation to achieve a certain visual effect.  The distinctive characteristics of this data allow a machine learning model to be trained to predict the accurate camera internal parameters from a single, unlabelled image.  This model is then capable of calibrating a variety of eye-to-hand cameras with semi-flexible lenses, regardless of the specific camera model or camera sensor used.  Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by showing improved object segmentation and object pose estimation performance when using the eye-to-hand dataset that has been adjusted with the internal parameters set by the machine learning model.

High-resolution solutions are crucial in inverse problems, especially when reconstructing medical images for a more accurate diagnosis and effective treatment. One approach to solving this problem is using generative adversarial networks (GANs) which can generate conditional images. However, training these models can be challenging and they tend to underfit the data, generating a limited range of conditions. A proposed solution is a modified $f$-divergence gain that regularizes the model and penalizes unobserved conditions, enabling it to sample from the same distribution as the training data. When tested in an imaging reconstruction scenario, this new divergence outperformed other training methods and provided the best results.
This article examines the possibility of invariant solutions in dynamical systems where the progression is measured in fractions of a unit of time.

Next-generation wireless networks, utilizing Terahertz frequencies, are being explored to overcome 5G capacity limitations, by utilizing short-distance, direct links. However, due to rapid signal degradation at THz frequencies, beyond a few meters, more flexible and longer-distance communication is required. Sub-wavelength beam training is being proposed to allow choosing multiple beams per antenna sector, but results in an enormous search space that hampers efficient packet-based beam training algorithms. This paper investigates reinforcement learning applications for selecting optimal beams in direct, single-hop THz links, demonstrating its potential to learn effective beam selection patterns with minimal or no data. The paper also evaluates the algorithm's performance in non-line-of-sight environments, by utilizing intermediate devices to create multi-hop paths.

The interstellar medium is being studied by analyzing the scintillation patterns of radio waves from bright pulsars, with a focus on small-scale fluctuations in electron density. By examining the scintillation patterns of the fast pulsar PSR B1133+16, which is very bright, researchers have created a detailed map of electron density fluctuations along its line of sight. They found that the size of these fluctuations changes with observing frequency, which can be explained by a two-screen model of scattering. However, this model is not fully supported by the data, suggesting a more complex structure may be present. Furthermore, the scattering screens are located at different distances from the Earth, with one screen located in our galaxy and the other in another galaxy. This indicates that the environment around the pulsar is very diverse and may be influenced by different types of stellar activity in the region.

This paper presents a new generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) to enhance the diversity of music generated by music synthesis models.  Music synthesis models are used to create virtual musical sounds, but their generated output is often of poor quality due to limited diversity.  Deep learning-based music synthesis synthesis models are typically trained to replicate the statistical patterns of recordings, resulting in blurry and diverse sounds.  In contrast, quasi-periodic sounds characteristic of musical instruments require more precise modeling.  To address this issue, we propose QPNet, a sequence-to-x model that predicts musical instrument sounds directly from textual descriptions.  QPNet incorporates a novel Quasi-Periodic Multi-Term Truncated Fourier Cosine Series (QPT-FCS) decoder and an innovative dilated convolution neural network (DCNN) unit designed to capture the temporal structure of musical tones and preserve their sharp onsets and decay.  Furthermore, our proposal includes an improved dataset called Quasi-Periodic Speech (QPS) to facilitate the comprehensive evaluation of QPEN's performance.  Experimental results show that QPNet is capable of producing sounds that closely resemble the sounds of musical instruments, outperforming the state-of-the-art sequence-to-x model in terms of objective quality metrics.

Historically, Semitic languages such as Arabic have followed a root-pattern system instead of the more common triconsonantal pattern. As a result, analyzing and annotating Arabic words from a morphological perspective has proven to be a complex and challenging task. This study presents a new, user-friendly web application called MADARi, which is designed to facilitate a range of Arabic morphological analysis tasks including automatic and manual pattern identification, automatic and manual root extraction, and the use of a pattern-based markup approach. MADARi is an evolution of its predecessor, an earlier version of the platform was previously showcased during the 2019 Shared Task on Arabic Root and Pattern Annotation. This study highlights the technical advancements of MADARi, which now boasts a more efficient pattern and root matching tool, an expanded vocabulary list, and a user-friendly interface for managing large-scale annotation projects.

The photochemistry of temperate terrestrial exoplanets has not been thoroughly investigated due to a lack of photochemical data from solar system terrestrial planets. This study presents a comprehensive framework for analyzing photochemistry in rocky exoplanets with Earth-like or Venus-like atmospheres. Using a newly developed model, we simulate the effects of solar radiation on atmospheric composition and temperature, as well as spectral analysis of these planets. It can also be applied to planets affected by shortwave radiation from their host stars. Assuming Earth-like atmospheres for Earth-orbiting exoplanets, we observe ozone formation only after a certain point where the planet's atmosphere is fully exposed to sunlight. Ozone formation is sensitive to atmospheric conditions and can be influenced by the presence of nitrogen molecules. Ozone formation is also observed in the atmospheres of Mars and Phobos, despite their unique orbital dynamics. Additionally, ozone formation is observed in the atmospheres of Mars and Phobos, even though they are subject to intense solar radiation.

To differentiate between zero-energy peaks caused by Majorana and other mechanisms like trivial or Kondo peaks, a novel approach is suggested: tunneling spectroscopy with resistive barriers exhibiting Ohmic damping. Using a Bragg mirror to model this setup, findings indicate that the spectral lineshape is primarily dictated by the damping strength. A key threshold emerges: when the energy gap significantly exceeds this strength, clear in-gap peaks are observed, but as the strength increases, these in-gap peaks display distinct characteristics unique from tunneling with power-law distributions or saturated cases.

The development of advanced detection technologies and the rapid expansion of urban areas have accelerated the identification of road problems such as surface cracks, potholes, and various infrastructure defects. While numerous studies and data sets exist in this area, there's a need to streamline the process of collecting, cleaning, and analyzing this information for consistent and accurate highway defect detection through automated methods. To address this challenge, a comprehensive tool called RoadAtlas has been developed, providing a standardized framework for annotation, data management, and the development of artificial intelligence models to detect a broad spectrum of road abnormalities. Utilizable by both industry professionals and researchers, RoadAtlas facilitates the creation of custom detection systems and inquires on its capabilities through an intuitive graphical interface.

This study offers a new categorical definition of shadows that aligns with the principles of higher-dimensional mathematics. Specifically, we demonstrate that shadows correspond to a bicategorical equivalent of ' slices ' within the framework of 2-categories. Furthermore, this relationship is preserved under the application of pseudofunctors.
This study aims to localize sounds using a challenging method.

This research presents a novel type of graph neural network called Lorentzian Graph Neural Networks (LGNNs), which employ a Lorentzian activation function to mitigate the limitations of the ReLU activation function. The ReLU activation function, widely used in traditional graph neural networks like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Transformer models, contributes positively to optimization but causes the hierarchical separation issue due to its lack of continuity. The LGNNs, in contrast, offer an alternative that maintains enhanced continuity while mitigating the hierarchical separation problem. Furthermore, LGNNs exhibit superior performance in certain tasks that require precise classification, such as node attribute prediction, outperforming ReLU-based models like R-GAT. Additionally, LGNNs demonstrate improved robustness against adversarial attacks, resulting in greater accuracy and stability.

This research model is mathematically described as a structural acoustic interaction,
where an oscillating component makes contact with a fixed apparatus in the following ways:
- No engagement occurs when the components do not come into contact.
- A purely normal engagement is modeled when the interacting component is positioned
  perpendicular to the fixed apparatus.
- An edge engagement is modeled if the interacting component is positioned at a right
  angle to the fixed apparatus.

In optics, compressing light into optical cavities is a common and well-documented phenomenon. A question arises whether the same applies to mechanics, specifically about the ability to compress mechanical resonators and whether this is achievable through optomechanical coupling. We investigate the option of generating a steady-state optomechanical state that is compressed in both optical and mechanical modes through the coupling of the two modes. By analyzing a system with two optomechanical modes connected in a loop, and considering various configurations of the system, including an increase in optical nonlinearity, we examine the feasibility of creating such a hybrid state. Our study reveals that while there are limitations, it is indeed possible to create an optomechanical state that exhibits compression in both modes.

This research extends both scalar and vectorial basic mu-calculus by incorporating a form of differentiation known as the directional derivative, resulting in a advanced framework that can be considered as a sort of vectorial mu-calculus. An alternative interpretation is offered in this extension before a key result is demonstrated: any program in this expanded framework can be simplified to an expression in the standard basic mu-calculus.

We introduce a novel efficient exponential delay discounting model that aligns with the Tsallis framework. It utilizes the delayed intrinsic energy concept and the parameterized intrinsic probability to derive the Tsallis distribution, allowing for the derivation of the efficient exponential delay discounting model. The delay discounting factor can be expressed as the function of the delayed intrinsic energy, and the framework's implications include the establishment of the uncertainty principle, the momentum distribution, the general Gibbs variational principle, and the general Fenchel-Moreau theorem. Furthermore, the general delay discounting Hamilton-Jacobi equation and the general delay discounting Euler-Lagrange equation are obtained within this energy-dependent Tsallis probability-derived framework.

Hachisu's proposed Harmonic Gauge gains traction in Substantial Gravity due to the derivation of Newton's limit, the suitability of the post-Newtonian expansion, and the correlation with the Equivalence Principle. The harmonic gauge's freedom allows for the proposal of specific Harmonic Gauge conditions that may facilitate the further development of gravitational theory.

We investigate the concept of extended double covers for signed graphs and prove a new theorem on homomorphism limits of these structures. A key consequence of this theorem is the identification of infinite families of signed graphs that exhibit no homomorphisms to any transitive orientation of their directed counterparts, despite having increasingly large transitive orientations as directed graphs. Additionally, our results provide a broader framework for analyzing directed graph coloring limits in relation to directed graph orientations.

The Weyl-Wigner representation has been utilized to translate the canonical equilibrium equations into a form that applies to both quantum and classical systems. This representation reveals the non-local nature of quantum correlations through deviations from the classical behavior, which can be quantified by the order of the relevant $\hbar$ terms in the expansion. The same order can be reached in the semi-classical expansion of the free energy, whose WW transform can be expressed as the sum of the classical parts and quantum corrections.

The notion of negative absolute temperature, initially proposed by Lambert in 1900 and later developed by Gibbs in 1902 and Gibbs in 1906, has seen a renewed interest due to the 2011 experiment by S. B. Wilkenston et al., which claimed to have synthesized a substance with negative temperature. A careful examination of this system, as well as its predecessors, reveals that the authors have not fully addressed the fundamental differences between the partition functions used in classical and quantum statistics, which directly impacts the nature of negative temperature. When applying the correct quantum statistics, we find that the system's entropy would actually increase with energy, contradicting the negative temperature observation. This issue arises from the system's inability to account for the Pauli exclusion principle, which, if considered, results in an infinite heat capacity at the Fermi temperature, rendering the system unstable and incapable of achieving negative temperatures.

Evaluating colorectal polyps histologically is crucial for cancer prevention.
However, the difficult task of dysplasia evaluation from whole-slide images is often done by dividing the slides into small patches for easier processing.
Recently, advances in artificial intelligence have led researchers to develop methods to evaluate polyps directly, thus avoiding issues caused by patching.
In this study, a new dataset called UniToPatho is introduced, containing 149 annotated whole-slide images of colorectal polyps obtained from routine R&D activities at UniToPatho S.r.l.
This is the second public histological dataset for whole-slide polyp evaluation after PaCo.
Additionally, UniToPatho is one of the first public datasets with private metadata to support the development and testing of proprietary technologies in collaboration with academic institutions.

This research introduces a novel finite element method to address wave equation problems with variable wavenumbers and source terms that vary in space. The approach addresses the challenge of numerical instability that arises due to the large magnitude of $k^2$ in the equation. Assuming the source and medium boundaries are smooth, it is demonstrated that for a range of high-frequency applications, elements with larger sizes than the wavelength can effectively provide an accurate and precise solution. Furthermore, it is found that as the frequency increases, the method can even become more efficient with fewer and larger computational elements, contrary to conventional expectations.

New data points, specifically the 18O isotopic ratios and water contents of pyroxenes and feldspars in Chelyabinsk and Benenitra H chondrites, suggest remarkably high values, up to 0.68 wt.%, of deuterium-enriched water within these meteorites. Notably, the oxygen isotopic ratios in the Chelyabinsk sample align with the DMM mantle endmember, indicating their origin from the Earth's mantle. Based on mineral water content, the water in Chelyabinsk and Benenitra is believed to have been trapped during the impact that formed these meteorites. If this interpretation holds true, it would mean the target rocks affected by the Chelyabinsk impact were already significantly hydrated before the event. Given that meteorites from Chelyabinsk and Benenitra exhibit indicators of low-moisture impacts, it is proposed that the building blocks of our early solar system likely contained a substantial amount of ice during their formation.

Using the thermodynamic-limite approach, we calculated the long-wavelength energy and momentum for a particular type of spin chain called the affine XXZ chain. These calculations were done for any kind of higher-spin interaction and for any combination of anisotropy and twist parameters. The results led to a general formula that defines the affine quantum-algebra symmetry of the XXZ spin chain in a quantizable Lax operator within an arbitrary representation. This new expression is also connected to form-factor expressions derived by Basu and Ghoshal for affine form factors of the TQ-relation of the XXZ quantum spin chain.

This paper introduces a novel concept called zero-shot voice translation, which enables the translation of any spoken language into any other language without necessitating a matching language pair. In a surprising finding, we discovered that existing models can achieve meaningful cross-lingual translation without any prior exposure to the involved language pairs. Building on this discovery, we developed a new approach called universal voice translation, which tailors a single model to produce output that adheres to the acoustic characteristics of the language being translated. We surpassed the previous record for the challenging task of voice translation by a significant margin of 5 dB on the most difficult dataset.

To enhance the efficiency of optical influence computations in many-body systems, a new multipolar decomposition scheme is introduced. This method circumvents the limitations of the dipole approximation associated with scattering and optical response calculations. The efficiency of this method is significantly improved by implementing a fast multipole expansion of the 3D volume and surface operations. The introduced method is not constrained by a small kd parameter, enabling precise optical response simulations even with incident wavelengths comparable to the volume and surface dimensions. This approach is demonstrated using a 3D cube model and successfully replicates exact results with a minimal computational cost, requiring only a small fraction of the cycles needed for traditional methods.

This study introduces the concept of double Young-Capelli bitableaux and associated altered Schur functions to extend the work of Laumon and Schur around 1890. Additionally, we define quantum Young-Capelli bases for quantum $GL(n)$ invariants of multiloop graphs and establish a connection between these and altered Schur numbers.

Within the most minimal scoto-seesaw model, we examine the predicted dark matter behavior, specifically its consistency with observational data and theoretical implications for neutrino mass. Neutrino data suggest a dark matter mass in the 20-4000 GeV scope, with model parameters aligned with LHC data for a majority of this range. However, precision electroweese measurements impose a more restrictive dark matter mass of 2.4-54 Geve, disallowing the heavier WIMP dark matter envisioned in the standard minimal scoto-seesaw model.

The concept of spin-orbit coupling has gained significant attention in the study of 5d transition metal compounds due to their large interelectronic and spin-orbit couplings. To better understand the electronic properties of these materials, researchers employed a method using local basis functions to represent the hybridization between 4d/5d $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ electron orbitals in a tight-binding Hamiltonian. By utilizing this approach, they were able to accurately reproduce the total energy and local electron density obtained from more complex ab initio calculations, specifically density functional theory. Furthermore, this model was capable of representing the effects of hybridization on the total energy in a straightforward and intuitive manner.

In this study, we extend the Lagrangian Floer cohomology to certain altered complex manifolds, including blow-ups. For modified manifolds with specific features, we define a new homological invariant, the R-Floer homology, that remains consistent under change. This preservation allows the homology of the altered manifold to be related to that of its pre-alteration. Additionally, we show that if the alteration is a creant transformation, the Floer homologies are directly equivalent. These findings enable the transfer of persistent homology data from the deformation space of a manifold to its moduli space of stable maps.

Diagnosing and treating various diseases relies on medical imaging, which has made deep learning a crucial tool. Deep learning models for analysis and intervention have become an important aspect of this process. Although some progress has been made in image interpretation, creating realistic images for testing purposes remains an unrealized goal. This paper outlines the objectives and initial findings of a project aimed at using advanced techniques to modify X-rays in a way that reflects specific medical conditions, enabling more comprehensive testing and exploring the potential for images to influence decision-making.

This note introduces ViDaExpert, a intuitive tool for examining and visualizing multidimensional vectors across various fields, including computer vision and robotics.  The tool employs nonlinear dimensionality reduction techniques to create compact representations that preserve the original data structure, followed by an interactive 3D visualization using immersive technologies like Virtual Reality headsets.  By combining these features, ViDaExpert enables researchers to efficiently explore complex datasets and identify significant patterns or anomalies, expediting the prototyping process for advanced systems, such as dexterous robot hands.

This paper introduces the novel concept of Newtonian potential smoothness in relation to Newton's inverse square law on flat domains in R^d. We express the fractional Laplacian of the Newtonian potential as a multiplicative constant times the unit measure on a flat domain, providing a precise characterization of its nonlinearity. Our proof relies on showing that the fractional Laplacian of the Riesz potential f_{d-2} equals f times the constant, given that the domain has finite D^s norm. Additionally, we derive similar results for boundary values of Newtonian potentials on bounded domains in R^d.
